title: Hotels Are Losing Two-Thirds of Their Bookings — Here's the Real Cost
hook_line: An independent hotel loses 63% of its bookings to Booking.com and Expedia before a guest ever sees its own website.
cliffhanger_line: That's before you even get to what a bad guest experience costs them on top of it — and the real fix isn't what you'd think.
pinned_comment: Full breakdown — including how much this actually costs a real hotel — is in the full episode. Link in description.
why: Opens on the headline stat (63.4% loss, cancellation gap) and the $135K arithmetic, then cuts before naming the fix (the agent stack) — keeps viewers wanting the resolution only the long-form has.

title: Nobody in This Industry Publishes a Price. That's the Whole Story.
hook_line: Every company that fixes hotel revenue for a living hides its price.
cliffhanger_line: That's not a hole in the research. That's the finding — and it changes what you'd actually charge for this.
pinned_comment: Why that pricing gap matters (and what to do about it) is in the full episode. Link in description.
why: Sets up the private-pricing pattern across four named vendors as an unresolved puzzle, ends on the implication without stating what to actually charge — the playbook lives only in long-form.

title: A Hotel Website Doesn't Get You Direct Bookings. It Just Sits There.
hook_line: Build it and they will come is not true for hotel bookings — and small hotels don't have the bandwidth to fix that themselves.
cliffhanger_line: That's the job nobody on staff had time for. What actually does it isn't a person.
pinned_comment: The three-agent system that replaces that job is in the full episode. Link in description.
why: Names the real gap (manpower/skillset, not a website problem) and teases that something non-human fills it, without revealing the specific agent roles — pulls viewers to long-form for the mechanism.

title: I Ran This Exact Flow With 50 People. A Solo B&B Owner Doesn't Have That.
hook_line: At Coqui Coqui, getting a guest from a social post to a booking to check-in took a team of fifty.
cliffhanger_line: A single-operator bed-and-breakfast doesn't have that headcount. Here's what stands in for it.
pinned_comment: What replaces a 50-person team for a solo operator — the full agent breakdown is in the episode. Link in description.
why: Personal founder-credibility hook (direct operator experience at Coqui Coqui) makes the stakes concrete, then teases the solution without naming it — the information gap holds until the viewer clicks through.
